note: Site dates for Wrest Park, used for all date arithmetic (rulers come from the reference pack). from/to are years; approx = date is circa; born/died for people (with month where known); stops = tour stops where the thing is; who = who made it; related/people = links used to widen a question's facts.
owners: Leofnoth, a thegn, in the time of Edward the Confessor (if the Domesday manor is Wrest, as the Victoria County History takes it)
after the Norman Conquest, Hugh, holding of Walter, brother of Saher, as recorded in Domesday Book in 1086 (the identification with Wrest is the Victoria County History's)
holders not recorded; the manor was held of the barony of Wahull, and J. H. Round suggested it reached the Greys through an heiress
Reginald de Grey, 1st Baron Grey de Wilton
John de Grey, 2nd Baron Grey de Wilton
Roger de Grey, 1st Baron Grey of Ruthin (Wrest settled on him in 1311; the rest of the Bedfordshire property came to him in 1323)
Reginald Grey, 2nd Baron Grey of Ruthin
Reginald Grey, 3rd Baron Grey of Ruthin
Edmund Grey, 4th Baron Grey of Ruthin, Earl of Kent from 1465
George Grey, 2nd Earl of Kent (died in December 1503 by the Victoria County History and the Complete Peerage; December 1505 by Bedfordshire Archives)
Richard Grey, 3rd Earl of Kent, a spendthrift who was forced to sell Wrest
Sir Henry Wyatt, a Tudor royal councillor, who bought it from Richard Grey (a deed of 1514 describes it as a mortgage)

Sir Henry Grey, Richard's half-brother, who bought Wrest and neighbouring manors back in 1512 (Bedfordshire Archives also gives 28 April 1514); the rightful 4th Earl of Kent, though he never took the title
Reginald Grey, his grandson, recognised as 5th Earl of Kent in 1572
Henry Grey, 6th Earl of Kent
Charles Grey, 7th Earl of Kent
Henry Grey, 8th Earl of Kent, and his wife Elizabeth Talbot
Anthony Grey, 9th Earl of Kent, a cousin and country clergyman
Henry Grey, 10th Earl of Kent, and his wife Amabel Benn, the 'Good Countess'
Anthony Grey, 11th Earl of Kent (a boy at first, with his mother Amabel running the estate), and from 1663 his wife Mary, Baroness Lucas
Henry Grey, 12th Earl of Kent, Duke of Kent from 1710
Jemima, Marchioness Grey, his granddaughter, with her husband Philip Yorke, 2nd Earl of Hardwicke from 1764 (died 1790)
Amabel, Baroness Lucas, her elder daughter, Countess de Grey from 1816
Thomas Philip, 2nd Earl de Grey, her nephew
Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, his daughter
Francis, 7th Earl Cowper, her son
Auberon Herbert, 9th Baron Lucas, his nephew (let to the American ambassador Whitelaw Reid from 1905)
Nan Herbert, 10th Baroness Lucas, his sister, who sold the estate

John George Murray of Thirsk, chairman of north-eastern brewery and coal companies, who bought the house and most of the estate in 1917 (Bedfordshire Archives also says parts were sold off in 1918 and 1919)
the Sun Insurance Office, which bought the mansion and about 260 acres in 1939 and made it its wartime head office (Murray kept the rest of the estate)

the state (the Ministry of Works and its successors), which bought it about 1946 (Bedfordshire Archives says October 1949) and leased it to the National Institute of Agricultural Engineering, later Silsoe Research Institute
the state, with the house and gardens cared for and opened by English Heritage

things.name: the present house
things.who: designed by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, for himself, with James Clephan as clerk of works

things.name: the Orangery
things.who: designed by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, for himself, with James Clephan as clerk of works (about 1835 in the listing; 1838–1839 in a Historic England research report)

things.name: the Archer Pavilion
things.who: designed by Thomas Archer for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent; the Great Room painted by Hauduroy in 1712

things.name: the Pavilion's painted Great Room
things.who: painted in trompe-l'œil by Hauduroy, who signed it 'Hauduroy pinxit 1712'

things.name: the statue of William III
things.who: thought to be by the sculptor John Cheere, put up while Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, owned Wrest

things.name: the old house's demolition
things.who: carried out by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, while his new house was built; watercolours show parts still standing in 1838, and Bedfordshire Archives says the last parts went in 1840

things.name: the Long Water
things.who: made for Anthony, 11th Earl of Kent, and his wife Mary, with his mother Amabel; extended and given its Pavilion by Henry, Duke of Kent, in the early 1700s. The exact date is uncertain: early 1680s (English Heritage) or before 1685 (a 2013 survey)

things.name: the Duke's Great Garden
things.who: laid out for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, with the architects Nicholas Hawksmoor and Thomas Archer, and Batty Langley and William Kent; English Heritage dates it from 1706 into the 1720s

things.name: Earl de Grey's time as First Lord of the Admiralty
Earl de Grey becoming first President of the Institute of British Architects
Earl de Grey's time as Lord Lieutenant of Ireland
the 'river' canals
things.who: dug for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent; reshaped in 1758–1760 by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown for Jemima, Marchioness Grey, and her husband Philip Yorke

things.name: Capability Brown's reshaping of the canals
things.who: carried out by Lancelot 'Capability' Brown for Jemima, Marchioness Grey, and her husband Philip Yorke

things.name: the Capability Brown column
things.who: attributed to the architect Edward Stevens; dated 1760 in the listing, but Historic England's 2018 research suggests about 1769–1771

things.name: the Bath House
things.who: designed by Edward Stevens for Jemima, Marchioness Grey

things.name: the Glorious Revolution
the de Grey family's time at Wrest
things.who: the Greys: barons, then Earls of Kent from 1465, then the Duke of Kent, Jemima, Marchioness Grey, Amabel, Countess de Grey, and the 2nd Earl de Grey, then his Cowper and Lucas heirs, until the estate was sold in 1917

things.name: the first record of the Greys at Wrest
things.who: of Reginald de Grey holding one fee in Flitton and Silsoe of John de Wahull; papers made at his death in 1307–1308 list a 'capital messuage with a dovecote', thought to be the beginning of the house

things.name: Edmund Grey's creation as Earl of Kent
things.who: Edward IV's reward to Edmund Grey, who had changed to the Yorkist side at the Battle of Northampton in 1460 and was made Lord High Treasurer in 1463

things.name: the sale of Wrest
things.who: put up for sale by Nan Herbert, Baroness Lucas, after her brother Auberon was killed in 1916 and the house was damaged by fire; the buyer was John George Murray of Thirsk, a brewery and coal company chairman, in a private sale

things.name: the old house
things.who: the Greys' house from the first record of a 'capital messuage' in the 1280s, altered many times (a classical north front about 1671–1676, refaced fronts in 1791), until it was pulled down from 1834

things.name: the old house's classical north front
things.who: added for Anthony, 11th Earl of Kent, and his wife Mary, paid for largely from her inheritance of 1671, with Amabel keeping the accounts (the listing says 1671; Bedfordshire Archives 1672; the History of Parliament 1672 to 1676)

things.name: the Italian Garden
things.who: laid out for Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, beside the conservatory of his new house

things.name: the conservatory
things.who: built with the house for Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, with a glazed roof on ornate cast-iron trusses

things.name: the ornamental dairy
things.who: built as part of the service wing of Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey's new house

things.name: Le Petit Trianon playhouse
things.who: built in the grounds under Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, as a children's playhouse (the listing says for his children; his grandchildren seem likelier)

things.name: the French Parterre
things.who: laid out for Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, in the French style to go with his new house

things.name: the Mermaid Basin
things.who: thought by Historic England to have been put up by Francis, 7th Earl Cowper, between 1880 and 1904 (Bedfordshire Archives says mid-1800s, by the 2nd Earl de Grey)

things.name: Bowling Green House
things.who: remodelled by Batty Langley for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, on an earlier building (possibly an early-eighteenth-century deer house); the main walls are dated 1720–1721 by English Heritage

things.name: the West Half House
things.who: built for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, as a garden shelter; no architect is recorded

things.name: the East Half House
things.who: built for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, as a pair with the West Half House; the architect is unknown

things.name: the statue of the lady reading
things.who: probably made by John Cheere; Historic England says it shows Jemima, Marchioness Grey, but Bedfordshire Archives says the Duke of Kent's first wife, Jemima, who died in 1728

things.name: the Mithraic Altar
things.who: designed by Thomas Wright for Jemima, Marchioness Grey, and her husband Philip Yorke; its Greek inscription was written by Daniel Wray

things.name: the Hutton Monument
things.who: put up by Henry Grey, Duke of Kent, in memory of his friend Thomas Hutton

things.name: the five ancient altars
things.who: bought by Amabel, Countess de Grey, from T. Beauclere of Muswell Hill

things.name: the Chinese Temple
things.who: built for Jemima, Marchioness Grey, possibly to designs by William Chambers; Edward Stevens repaired it in 1769 and it was rebuilt or remodelled for Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, in 1876

things.name: the Chinese Bridge
things.who: designed by Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, and built by estate workmen, replacing a timber bridge of the 1760s

things.name: the sundial
things.who: made by Henry Wynne, a London instrument maker, as his plate signed and dated 1682 shows; the plate in the garden today is a replica

things.name: the six marble statues round the sundial
things.who: probably bought for Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, about 1840 (Bedfordshire Archives), or by his daughter Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, after 1859 (Historic England, which mentions the 1862 Exhibition)

things.name: the Atlas statue
things.who: a Portland stone figure of the early eighteenth century, probably one of Henry Grey, Duke of Kent's garden additions; the sculptor is unknown

things.name: the Sun Insurance Office's wartime move to Wrest
things.who: the Sun Insurance Office, which bought the estate in 1939 and moved its head office staff here from Threadneedle Street in London; the staff went back to London in 1945–1946, though Bedfordshire Archives says Sun only sold Wrest in October 1949

things.name: the agricultural engineering institute at Wrest
things.who: the National Institute of Agricultural Engineering, renamed Silsoe Research Institute in 1991, which leased the estate from the state (staff moved in between June 1947 and July 1948)

things.name: the driverless tractor work
things.who: begun at Reading University, whose tractor was first shown about 1958, then handed to the National Institute of Agricultural Engineering at Silsoe (the Silsoe dates are not recorded)

things.name: the camera-guided robot hoe
things.who: developed at Silsoe Research Institute by a team including Nick Tillett, Tony Hague and John Marchant

things.name: the restoration of the French Parterre
things.who: carried out by English Heritage to the Earl's design, after a full-area excavation in autumn 2011

things.name: the four lead statue groups on the parterre
things.who: attributed by Historic England to John Cheere and dated about 1730, though Cheere only set up his statue yard in 1739 and English Heritage dates one group to the late 1700s; in place by 1839

things.name: the start of the parterre statue restoration
things.who: begun by English Heritage, with conservators Skillington Workshop, on Venus and Adonis and Aeneas and Anchises

things.name: the Dairy Sculpture Gallery
things.who: made by English Heritage out of the ornamental dairy, to show garden statues too fragile to stay outdoors

things.name: the Silsoe entrance lodges
things.who: designed by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, his first buildings in the Louis XV style

things.name: the Petit Trianon at Versailles
things.who: designed by Ange-Jacques Gabriel for Louis XV, and given to Marie Antoinette by Louis XVI in 1774

things.name: the Crystal Palace
things.who: designed by Joseph Paxton for the Great Exhibition

things.name: the Great Conservatory at Chatsworth
things.who: designed by Joseph Paxton for the 6th Duke of Devonshire

things.name: Thomas Carew's poem 'To my friend G.N. from Wrest'
things.who: written by Thomas Carew while a guest of Henry, 8th Earl of Kent, and his wife Elizabeth Talbot, in spring 1639

things.name: the round fountain and its eight statues
things.who: acquired for Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, after she inherited in 1859, according to its listing; Bedfordshire Archives says about 1840 for Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey. The statues round it are early to mid nineteenth century on pedestals of the early 1700s

things.name: the statue of Mercury and Cupid
things.who: probably of the late 1600s, perhaps by Caius Gabriel Cibber, according to its listing (Bedfordshire Archives calls it mid nineteenth century); moved to the Long Water in the late nineteenth century

things.name: the lead urns at Bowling Green House
things.who: probably by John Van Nost the Younger, copies of carved urns by Edward Pearce and Cibber

things.name: the amphitheatre by the bowling green
things.who: added north of the bowling green during the Duke of Kent's works of 1729

things.name: the serpentine canal
things.who: made during the Duke of Kent's works of 1729; Capability Brown joined it to Old Park Water about 1760

things.name: John Rocque's plans of the garden
things.who: drawn by John Rocque, recording the Duke of Kent's gardens and garden buildings

things.name: the War of the Spanish Succession
things.who: fought by Britain, the Dutch Republic and the Habsburg Emperor against France and Spain over the Spanish throne; the Habsburg claimant was Archduke Charles

things.name: the Athenian Letters
things.who: written by a circle of friends around Philip Yorke and his brother Charles, including Daniel Wray, as letters from a Persian agent in Athens

things.name: Thomas Wright's Original Theory of the Universe
things.who: self-published by Thomas Wright of Durham in a very small printing

things.name: Immanuel Kant's Universal Natural History and Theory of the Heavens
things.who: published anonymously by Immanuel Kant, who had read a review of Thomas Wright's book

things.name: the Great Pagoda at Kew
things.who: designed by William Chambers for Princess Augusta

things.name: Chambers's Designs of Chinese Buildings
things.who: published in London by William Chambers

things.name: the lead statue of Diana and the greyhound
things.who: thought to be by Andrew Carpenter, bought for Henry Grey, Duke of Kent; sold away with Wrest in 1917 and bought back with Art Fund help in 2012

things.name: the carving of the five ancient altars
things.who: carved in Greek lands in the late Hellenistic period, the late second to first century BC; the maker is unknown

things.name: the repair of the Pavilion's lead dome
things.who: carried out by English Heritage to stop rain reaching the painted ceiling

things.name: the Bath House Cascade
things.who: built with the Bath House, over the spring head

things.name: the lead water pipes to the Bath House
things.who: ordered by the estate agent after wooden pipes kept failing in the boggy ground

things.name: the filling-in of the Bath House's bath
things.who: ordered by Earl de Grey after hot and cold baths were fitted in the old house

things.name: the 1960s restoration of the Bath House
things.who: carried out by the Ministry of Public Building and Works; it re-thatched the dressing room and dug out and rebuilt the bath

things.name: the pump that recirculates water to the Cascade
things.who: installed by the Ministry's engineers, as the Bath House spring had dried up

things.name: the raising of Old Park Weir
things.who: raised 6–10 inches in concrete to hold more water for the research institute's irrigation

things.name: the brewhouse, horse pump house and fire-engine house
things.who: designed by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, with James Clephan as clerk of works

things.name: the founding of the institute at Oxford
things.who: founded at the University of Oxford as the Institute of Agricultural Engineering, to run farm machinery trials and research

things.name: the institute's move to Askham Bryan
things.who: when the institute became a Ministry branch and was renamed the National Institute of Agricultural Engineering, in temporary quarters near York

things.name: the state's purchase of Wrest Park
things.who: bought by the Ministry of Works (called the Ministry of Public Building and Works in the Historic England entry) and leased to the agricultural engineering institute; the 2013 English Heritage report gives 1946 and also 1947, and Bedfordshire Archives says October 1949

things.name: the opening of the gardens to the public on summer weekends
things.who: opened by the Ministry of Works, according to a written answer in the House of Commons on 1 November 1960

things.name: the institute's transfer to the Agricultural Research Council
things.who: the move from the Ministry to the Agricultural Research Council, shifting the institute towards long-term research and away from routine testing

things.name: the renaming as Silsoe Research Institute
things.who: the AFRC Institute of Engineering Research (so called since 1986) took the more manageable name Silsoe Research Institute

things.name: the BBSRC's decision to end funding
things.who: the institute's main sponsor, the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council, deciding to stop supporting it because its own research priorities had changed

things.name: the closure of Silsoe Research Institute
things.who: the institute ceasing operations at the end of March 2006 after 80 years (Wikipedia's article on Silsoe says 2007)

things.name: the first sale of a camera-guided Robocrop hoe
things.who: built by Garford with the Silsoe camera guidance system, after the 1996 demonstration; Tillett and Hague Technology was set up after the closure was announced in 2005

things.name: the institute's tractor and machinery testing
things.who: carried out for the Ministry and manufacturers by the institute (the World Agricultural Tractor Trials of 1930 are the start the institute's history gives)

things.name: the institute's tests of tractor safety cabs
things.who: reported by the institute in test reports from 1963 (the Bonser cab) to 1971 (the County cab) in the Museum of English Rural Life catalogue

things.name: the Agriculture (Tractor Cabs) Regulations
things.who: made by the Minister of Agriculture and the Secretary of State for Scotland, requiring approved safety cabs on tractors driven by agricultural workers

things.name: the crop drying research
things.who: begun in the Oxford institute of 1924 and followed by grass-dryer and grain-dryer testing in the 1940s and 1950s

things.name: the spray drift research
things.who: reported to the British Crop Protection Council by Paul Miller of Silsoe Research Institute (the 1999 paper is one example, not the start of the work)

things.name: the Silsoe 6 m cube wind experiment
things.who: the full-scale cube results published by Hoxey, Richards and Short; the build year of the cube is not recorded here

things.name: Richard Grey's sale of Wrest to Sir Henry Wyatt
things.who: forced on Richard Grey, 3rd Earl of Kent, by his debts (the date is from the Inventories of Bedfordshire Country Houses; a deed of 1514 calls it a mortgage)

things.name: Henry Grey's buying back of Wrest
things.who: done by Sir Henry Grey, Richard's half-brother, who feared Wyatt would pull the house down; he paid 450 marks (£300). Bedfordshire Archives also gives 28 April 1514

things.name: Reginald Grey's recognition as Earl of Kent
things.who: granted by Elizabeth I, after the title had 'lain asleep' for about fifty years because Henry Grey could not afford to take it

things.name: the creation of the barony of Lucas of Crudwell
things.who: made for Mary, wife of Anthony, 11th Earl of Kent, by Charles II, with a rule that let it pass through women; this is how Wrest later passed to Jemima, Amabel and Anne Florence

things.name: Jemima's inheritance of Wrest
things.who: when Henry, Duke of Kent, died on 5 June 1740 with no surviving son; she had married Philip Yorke two weeks earlier, on 22 May 1740

things.name: Thomas, Earl de Grey's inheritance of Wrest
things.who: from his aunt Amabel, Countess de Grey, who died on 4 March 1833 (Bedfordshire Archives says 4 May)

things.name: Whitelaw Reid's tenancy of Wrest
things.who: the American ambassador, who rented Wrest from Lord Lucas at £1,500 a year from 1905 and stayed about eight years

things.name: King Edward VII's visit to Wrest
things.who: a weekend visit on 24–25 July 1909 as the guest of the ambassador Whitelaw Reid; the Bedfordshire Times called it the first visit by a sovereign to Wrest

things.name: the First World War hospital at Wrest
things.who: set up by Nan Herbert and her brother Lord Lucas, who paid for it; ready for patients on 7 September 1914 and about 1,600 men passed through

things.name: the 1916 fire at Wrest
things.who: on 14 September 1916; it badly damaged the mansion (a local account puts it in the east wing), all 156 patients were got out safely and the hospital never reopened

things.name: the 1917 auction of Wrest's contents
things.who: run on the premises by Messrs Foster from 10 September 1917 for five days

things.name: the sale of Wrest's statues under John George Murray
things.who: carried out in the 1930s by Murray, who moved to Coles Park in about 1932; the Four Seasons and Four Elements went to Ditchley Park and the Duke's obelisk and the Duchess's column to Trent Park

things.name: English Heritage's takeover of Wrest
things.who: after the Silsoe Research Institute closed at the end of March 2006; English Heritage began a 20-year restoration plan

things.name: the reopening of the restored gardens
things.who: on 4 August 2011, after restoration helped by the Heritage Lottery Fund and the Wolfson Foundation

things.name: English Heritage's archaeological collections store
things.who: a £2 million purpose-built store holding over 150,000 objects from English Heritage sites, opened to visitors in 2014
